title: Exercises · Question 2
html:
Question: Dynamic Obstacle Detection and Mapping for a Mobile Robot

Scenario:

A mobile robot is exploring an unknown indoor environment and must build a real-time obstacle map using multiple range sensors. The robot moves in a 10m × 10m grid, scanning its surroundings and marking detected obstacles.

The robot is equipped with the following sensors:

  • Ultrasonic Sensor (HC-SR04) – Detects nearby objects (within 1.5m)
  • LIDAR Sensor – Provides high-accuracy distance readings (up to 8m)
  • Time-of-Flight (ToF) Sensor – Detects fast-moving obstacles within 3m
  • Infrared (IR) Sensor – Detects low-reflectivity obstacles within 1m

Robot Movement and Mapping Process:

  1. The robot starts at position (0,0) in the 10m × 10m grid.
  2. It moves 1 meter per step, scanning for obstacles in its forward direction.
  3. If an obstacle is detected, the robot marks it on the map and chooses a new direction.
  4. The robot continues scanning and moving until it has explored the entire area or reaches a dead end.
  5. The program outputs the final obstacle map with detected objects marked as X.

Task:

Write a Python program that:

  1. Simulates range sensor readings (random distances).
  2. Moves the robot step by step, scanning for obstacles in its path.
  3. Marks detected obstacles (X) on a 10x10 grid.
  4. Prints the final obstacle map after the robot completes its exploration.

Hints:

  • Use a 2D list (matrix) to represent the 10x10 grid.
  • At each step, generate random sensor values and check if they are below obstacle thresholds.
  • If an obstacle is found, mark it as X and change direction.
  • If the robot cannot move in any direction, stop and print the final map.

  • It moves forward step by step, scanning for obstacles.
  • If any sensor detects an obstacle, it marks X on the grid and changes direction.
  • The final grid shows explored paths and detected obstacles.

How the Robot Moves:

  1. It starts at (0,0).
  2. Moves 1 step per iteration.
  3. Scans forward using Ultrasonic, LIDAR, ToF, and IR sensors.
  4. If an obstacle is detected, it marks X on the grid and chooses a new direction.
  5. Continues moving until the entire grid is explored or a dead end is reached.
